import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 115

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/115](https://www.erdosproblems.com/115)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er90] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990),
  467-478.
- [ErLe94] Erëmenko, A. and Lempert, L., *An extremal problem for polynomials*. Proc. Amer. Math.
  Soc. (1994), 191-193.
- [Po59a] Pommerenke, Ch., *On the derivative of a polynomial*. Michigan Math. J. (1959), 373-375.
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos115

/--
If $p(z)$ is a polynomial of degree $n$ such that $\{z : \lvert p(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ is connected
then is it true that
$$\max_{\substack{z\in\mathbb{C}\\ \lvert p(z)\rvert\leq 1}} \lvert p'(z)\rvert
\leq (\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))n^2?$$

Eremenko and Lempert [ErLe94] have shown this is true, and in fact Chebyshev polynomials are the
extreme examples.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos115.lean"]
theorem erdos_115 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ p : Polynomial ℂ, p.Monic → p.natDegree = n →
      IsConnected {z : ℂ | ‖p.eval z‖ ≤ 1} → ∀ z : ℂ, ‖p.eval z‖ ≤ 1 →
        ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ ≤ (1 / 2 + ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos115

findings.description: The theorem correctly assumes `p.Monic`, but its docstring only says that p is a polynomial of degree n. The omitted normalization is essential: for every positive n, pₙ(z) = (nz)^n has connected unit lemniscate {|z| ≤ 1/n} and |pₙ′(1/n)| = n², contradicting the unnormalized asymptotic bound. This is a documentation defect, not an error in the Lean statement. The unnormalized statement's negation was proved in the scratch file without using the reviewed theorem.
findings.source_evidence: Eremenko–Lempert, “An extremal problem for polynomials,” p. 191, explicitly starts with “Let f(z) = z^n + … be a polynomial” and imposes f(z) ~ z^n at infinity in condition (1): https://www.math.purdue.edu/~eremenko/dvi/lempert.pdf. Erdős [Er61], §IV.1, p. 246, likewise begins with a polynomial z^n + …: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1961-22.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to “If p(z) is a monic polynomial of degree n …”. Keep the Lean hypothesis `p.Monic`. The extremal examples can also be described as suitably normalized Chebyshev polynomials.

reformulations.difference: Lean replaces the source's maximum of |p′| on the unit lemniscate by an upper bound at every point of that lemniscate.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a nonconstant complex polynomial, the unit lemniscate is compact because polynomial evaluation is proper, and nonempty because the polynomial has a complex root. Continuity of |p′| therefore gives an attained maximum, whose upper bound is equivalent to the pointwise bound. The only monic degree-zero polynomial is 1; its derivative is identically zero, so the maximum still exists despite the lemniscate being all of ℂ. This equivalence, including the constant case, was proved as `pointwise_iff_maximum` in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses the uniform asymptotic coefficient 1/2 + o(1) through `∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop`, with the polynomial and point quantified inside the eventual statement.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On ℕ, this means that for each ε > 0 there is a threshold N, independent of p and z, beyond which the bound holds. This is the usual uniform meaning of the source's asymptotic upper bound. Conversely, choose strictly increasing thresholds N_k for ε = 1/k and use the corresponding piecewise-constant errors to obtain a vanishing error sequence. Allowing degree zero does not change an eventual statement. The threshold expansion was checked in Lean; a literal equivalence with an explicitly quantified vanishing-error sequence was not mechanized.

sources_consulted: Eremenko–Lempert, “An extremal problem for polynomials” (1994), pp. 191–193: https://www.math.purdue.edu/~eremenko/dvi/lempert.pdf
The cited external Lean proof, particularly its final theorem `Erdos115.eremenko_lempert_1999`: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plby/lean-proofs/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos115.lean
Erdős [Er90], Cambridge bibliographic/access page (full chapter unavailable): https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/CBO9780511983917A047/type/book_part
Pommerenke [Po59a], bibliographic record and full-text links (article downloads blocked): http://dml.mathdoc.fr/item/1028998284/

review.notes: No misformalization of the Lean theorem was found. The solved category and positive answer agree with Eremenko–Lempert's stronger bound 2^(1/n−1)n². The cited external proof states that sharp bound, and its implication to the reviewed asymptotic statement was independently proved in the scratch file. Its original Lean 4.29.1 project was not rebuilt. Boundary, nonvacuity, maximum-equivalence, and scaling checks compiled without sorryAx. The erdosproblems.com page remained Cloudflare-blocked despite descriptive user agents; the assessment instead uses the accessible primary papers. Er90's full chapter and Po59a's full article were unavailable, but their relevant correction and bound are explicitly discussed in ErLe94. No repository files were modified.
